meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.trans: A big city.
The sum is very large.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.trans: I'm not taking the knife.
Chef, I didn't take it.
We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
But you've still got some.
I told you: no.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I don't care.
Nobody cares.

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Too much to do.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

всякий.gloss: every kind of, all sorts of, any

meanings.en: every kind of, all sorts of, any
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?
examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Take it, just in case.
This is a strange case.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

вздумать.gloss: to take it into one's head; (neg.) don't even think about it

meanings.en: to take it into one's head; (neg.) don't even think about it
meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take it into one's head; (neg.) don't even think about it', paired with 'вздумывать'.

related.gloss: to take it into one's head
to to take it into one's head (prefixed perfective)
not to to take it into one's head (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Don't even think about it, son. There always was.
Don't even think about going there!

examples.text: Не вздумай, сынок. Всегда были. Сейчас найдём.
examples.trans: Don't even think about it, son. There always was. We'll find some now.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'weapon, arms' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Drop weapons! Hands behind head!
Drop your weapon right now!
The police confiscated the firearm.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трелять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to shoot, to fire', paired with 'выстрелить'.

examples.trans: Surrender, enemy! I am shooting!
Who is shooting in the forest?
The soldiers are shooting at targets.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.

examples.trans: Don't worry.
I'm nervous.
Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

пугать.gloss: to scare, to try to frighten

meanings.en: to scare, to try to frighten
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to scare, to try to frighten', paired with 'напугать'.

examples.trans: I scared him properly, sternly!
Don't scare the child.

examples.text: А ты таким голосом его и пугал?
examples.trans: And did you try to scare him in that voice?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Release him immediately!
Go home at once.
What bribe? Release him immediately!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.trans: Call the police!
The police are here.

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to figure out
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.
I'll figure everything out soon.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bartender' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The bartender poured the wine.

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is this our car now?
Which car did you come in?
A car. A German one.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.
Let him say it.

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride', paired with 'поехать'.

examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем?
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'otherwise', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go, or else you'll be late.
I think differently.

examples.text: Пятьдесят метров, не больше. Иначе будет сигнал.
examples.trans: Fifty metres, no more. Otherwise there'll be a signal.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, foolishness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What nonsense?
Don't talk nonsense.

examples.text: Что за глупости? Значит, Осипенко сам эти деньги украл!
examples.trans: What nonsense? That means Osipenko stole that money himself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'творить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do (something bad), cause trouble', paired with 'творить'.

examples.trans: What have you done?
Look at what they've done here!

examples.text: Что ты натворил? — Марина, он врёт, он симулянт!
examples.trans: What have you done? — Marina, he's lying, he's a faker!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to smoke'.

examples.trans: Drop the cigarette! Smoking is very harmful!

examples.text: За то, что курите слишком часто!
examples.trans: Because you smoke far too often!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'walks'.

examples.text: Мальчик ходит на костылях. А она ещё и активистка.
examples.trans: The boy walks on crutches. And she's an activist, too.

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.
examples.trans: She was the one who met me! She circled around me like a shark.
She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

заодно.gloss: at the same time, while I'm at it

meanings.en: at the same time, while I'm at it
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'одно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: And at the same time I'll trim the branches in the yard.
Buy bread and milk while you're at it.

examples.text: Заодно без лишних ушей обсудим твоё назначение.
examples.trans: At the same time without extra ears we will discuss your appointment.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'литка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'snail, escargot' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And took the snails out for a walk at the same time?
And here are the snails.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гуливать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to walk (a dog)'.

examples.trans: And took the snails out for a walk at the same time?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет выгуливать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to walk without a reason.
